summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Borisoglebsk airbase in Voronezh Oblast, destroying six Su-34 bombers with Neptune missiles and causing a major fire. points: Ukrainian forces conducted a strike on the Borisoglebsk military airbase in Voroneezh Oblast, Russia, destroying six Su-34 bombers using Neptune cruise missiles and triggering a large-scale fire at the facility. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/76944)

President Zelenskyy announced Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, ending a three-day pause, citing ongoing Russian attacks that killed over 100 civilians in the past week. (Source: @UkraineNow/84666)

Kirovohrad region endured over 10 hours of mass drone attacks, resulting in three fatalities and six injuries, with 25 locations hit and residential infrastructure damaged. (Source: @UkraineNow/84670)

In Kyiv's Pecherskyi District, debris from a downed drone struck near a residential building, injuring five people and damaging the building facade and windows, with a car catching fire. (Source: @UkraineNow/84671)

Ukraine's Defense Forces attacked the Borisoglebsk airbase in Voronezh Oblast, where Su-34, Su-35C, and Su-30SM aircraft are stationed and used to drop guided bombs on Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/84664)

A drone attack on a store in Odesa region partially destroyed the building and damaged vehicles, leaving three injured; President Zelenskyy called it a demonstrative response by Russia to signals from the US. (Source: @UkraineNow/84675)
Ukraine has exhausted its supply of Patriot interceptor missiles, according to CNN, with the shortage lasting several months and affecting air defense capabilities. (Source: @UkraineNow/84682)

Russian forces launched a large-scale drone and missile offensive targeting multiple Ukrainian regions including Kyiv, Chernihiv, Vinnytsia, and Odesa, with Geran-5 missiles and Shahed drones detected across several directions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/76941)

The Borisoglebsk military airbase in Voronezh Oblast was struck by Ukrainian forces, destroying six Su-34 bombers and causing a major fire, with the base housing Su-34, Su-35C, and Su-30SM aircraft. (Source: @UkraineNow/84664)
Russian Foreign Intelligence Director Sergei Naryshkin and FBI Director Christopher Wray visited Russia, though the purpose and details of their meetings remain unclear. (Source: @UkraineNow/84660)

Elon Musk stated that Starlink restrictions on Ukraine are not under his control, noting that Starshield belongs to the US government and limitations may be imposed by military officials or former President Trump. (Source: @UkraineNow/84663)
Russian forces destroyed a logistics terminal in Dnipro, though no casualties were reported from the attack. (Source: @UkraineNow/84680)

Russian state media and propagandists, including Vladimir Solovyov, were involved in promoting Chinese automaker Changan Hunter Plus vehicles used by Russian military forces, according to investigative journalists. (Source: @UkraineNow/84669)

Russian naval forces experienced a setback in the Ormuz Strait when a Singaporean-flagged container ship sank after a mine explosion, losing over 2500 containers of electronic goods including iPhones. (Source: @eRadarrua/123235)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces continue to escalate aerial attacks across Ukraine, deploying Geran-5 missiles and Shahed drones in coordinated waves targeting multiple regions simultaneously. The destruction of six Su-34 bombers at Borisoglebsk airbase represents a significant degradation of Russian air capabilities, though Moscow is likely to retaliate with intensified strikes. Ukraine's depletion of Patriot interceptor missiles poses a critical vulnerability in defending against future Russian aerial assaults. The resumption of strikes on Russian oil refineries by Kyiv signals a potential escalation in energy infrastructure targeting. Regional actors should prepare for increased civilian casualties and infrastructure damage as both sides intensify their campaigns.
sections.regional_response: European leaders are urged to expedite military aid deliveries, particularly air defense systems, as Ukraine faces critical shortages of Patriot interceptor missiles. Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković has called for EU nations to share intelligence data with Ukraine if the US reduces cooperation. The US and its allies must coordinate a unified response to prevent further escalation, including potential sanctions on entities facilitating Russian military operations. NATO members should enhance air policing missions along eastern flanks to deter further Russian aggression. International maritime security in the Black Sea and Ormuz Strait requires heightened vigilance following recent incidents.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian intelligence successfully identified and targeted the Borisoglebsk airbase, demonstrating precise operational planning and execution capabilities. Russian electronic warfare systems appear to be struggling with Ukrainian drone incursions, as evidenced by multiple successful strikes. The involvement of Chinese-made vehicles in Russian military operations suggests deeper logistical ties between Moscow and Beijing. Disinformation campaigns are likely to intensify, with Russian state media potentially amplifying narratives around the Ormuz Strait incident. Monitoring of Starlink communications restrictions remains critical, as any limitations could impact Ukrainian battlefield coordination and civilian connectivity.
